category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: Tenant has no rent receipts but bank statements
expected: Explains that verified bank statements with beneficiary account details serve as admissible evidence under Indian Evidence Act.
prompt: The landlord never gave rent receipts, but I transferred rent to his bank account every month.
raw_response:
Hello, I understand how stressful it can be when a landlord does not provide rent receipts, but keeping digital records is a strong way to protect yourself.

### | Your Situation
You have been paying your monthly rent regularly through bank transfers to your landlord, but the landlord has failed to issue formal rent receipts for these payments. This documentation gap creates uncertainty regarding proof of rent payment and security deposit management under your tenancy.

### | Your Legal Position
- **Proof of Payment via Bank Transfer:** Under the Indian Evidence Act, digital bank statements showing regular monthly transfers to the landlord serve as valid financial records and primary evidence of rent payment, even in the absence of physical rent receipts.
- **Section 108(m) and (o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882:** You are bound to maintain the property subject only to reasonable wear and tear, and the landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions from your security deposit without proper contractual justification.
- **Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Guidelines & State Enactments) Section 11 & Section 13:** Security deposits are subject to statutory limits, and landlords are obligated to refund the deposit upon vacating, minus any valid, mutually agreed-upon deductions.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Download and save all your bank account statements clearly showing the monthly rent transfers made to the landlord's account.
2. Send written demand notice granting 15 days: Issue a formal written communication or demand notice to your landlord requesting the issuance of pending rent receipts for all completed payments and a clear accounting of the security deposit.
3. Appropriate forum e.g. Rent Authority: If the landlord refuses or attempts unfair deductions, you may approach the local Rent Authority or Rent Controller for dispute resolution.

### Information I still need from you
What is the monthly rent amount, and how long have you been renting this property?

citations.description: Strict grounds required for eviction; prohibits withholding essential amenities without reasonable cause. Tenant may approach Rent Controller for summary restoration.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
